chunks.rationale: Read grok.test.js first: the argv contract is the whole fix (asking modes must emit bypassPermissions + --always-approve, never auto). Then providers.test.js (same buildArgs assertion on the registry unit) and sandbox.test.js (badge copy tracks the flags we actually pass).
risks: Runner grok tests spawn a fake binary and only check argv; they do not prove grok 1.0.5 honors --always-approve. That was verified live against the real CLI.
plan mode is asserted to stay plan and not get --always-approve — a reviewer skimming only the default case could miss a plan-mode regression.

chunks.rationale: electron/providers.js grok.buildArgs is the spawn argv. This is where default/acceptEdits used to map to --permission-mode auto, which grok 1.0.5 treats as default and auto-cancels run_terminal_command as a user stop.
risks: default and acceptEdits on grok now fully auto-approve tools, indistinguishable from bypassPermissions. Headless -p cannot prompt anyway; the permission pill remains a no-op between those three modes (#177).

--always-approve and --permission-mode bypassPermissions are redundant on 1.0.5 (always-approve sets bypassPermissions). Both are passed because auto was the previous 'documented' mode and was silently ignored.
Already-running grok children keep the old argv until the next spawn; a live Solenta session will not pick this up mid-turn.

chunks.rationale: electron/sandbox.js only changes the badge reason string so it matches the flags buildArgs now emits. No confinement change (grok still has no --sandbox).
risks: If a future grok CLI honors auto again, the badge will still say bypassPermissions / --always-approve. That is honest about what we pass today.
This stops false 'Run stopped' from gated-tool auto-cancel. A real user Stop/Esc still goes through stopRun and still looks the same, which is correct.
plan mode can still auto-cancel gated tools in headless grok; we do not remap plan.
